tools.name: get_menu
tools.description: Get the full menu of a meni.ge location: categories, items with prices, variant groups and addons, currency and ordering capabilities. domain = uppercase location code from the QR/menu URL.

tools.name: get_item
tools.description: Get one menu item with its variant groups and addons, or several at once: pass itemIds (up to 10) instead of itemId to look items up in bulk — the bulk answer is {items, notFound}.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Semantic search over the location's catalog: product/dish names, descriptions, specifications, brand, SKU/barcodes and attached docs. Use for "do you have…" / "recommend…" / "how much is…" questions instead of paging through get_menu. Returns matching items with prices and a relevance score; falls b

tools.name: update_cart
tools.description: Build the guest order step by step in a server-side cart, the way a human uses the web cart. Without cartId a new cart is created (keep the returned cartId — it is the access token). Each entry of updates: {itemId, quantity, variants?, addons?, comment?} adds a line; {lineId, quantity} changes one;

tools.name: get_cart
tools.description: Read a cart created with update_cart: lines with live unit prices, subtotal, item count, the checkoutUrl for a human hand-off and the expiry date (carts live 7 days). Lines whose item left the menu are flagged unavailable and excluded from the subtotal.

tools.name: get_store_info
tools.description: Facts about the location that are not on the menu: address, contacts, coordinates, working hours with openNow computed in the venue timezone, delivery and pickup terms (fees, minimum order, zones, ETA), accepted payment methods and currency, shipping/return terms and links to the published legal doc

tools.name: search_policies_and_faqs
tools.description: Search the location's own published policies, FAQ entries and info pages (privacy, terms, returns, delivery, cookies, help articles) plus, when the owner allows it, their internal knowledge base. Returns short snippets with a link to the source. Use it for policy/help questions instead of guessing;

tools.name: create_order
tools.description: Validate and place an order at a meni.ge location. Returns orderId (keep it — it is the access token for status checks) and the computed total. customer.name/phone are required for pickup and delivery; delivery.address is required for delivery. tools.name: get_order_status
tools.description: Check the status of an order previously created with create_order.

tools.name: check_table_availability
tools.description: Which tables of the location are free or busy in a given time window (uses the floor plan published by the restaurant). Pass the chosen table id to create_reservation as tableId.

tools.name: create_reservation
tools.description: Request a table reservation. Starts as "pending" until the restaurant confirms — check with get_reservation_status. Returns reservationId (keep it: it is the token for status and cancellation). Optionally bind a specific table via tableId (from check_table_availability).

tools.name: get_reservation_status
tools.description: Status of a reservation created with create_reservation (pending/confirmed/seated).

tools.name: cancel_reservation
tools.description: Cancel a reservation previously created with create_reservation.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "get_store_info" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Facts about the location that are not on the menu: address, contacts, coordinates, working hours with openNow computed in the venue timezone, delivery and picku…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "search_policies_and_faqs" references sensitive artifacts (cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_item" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Get one menu item with its variant groups and addons." → after: "Get one menu item with its variant groups and addons, or several at once: pass itemIds (up to 10) instead of itemId to look items up in bulk — the bulk answer is {items, notFound}."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
